title: ‘Pirate Mo and the Legend of the Red Ruby’ Sails to More Than 50 Countries Ahead of AFM Premiere as Teaser Debuts (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Sales company The Playmaker Munich has closed further territory deals on animated family adventure film “Pirate Mo and the Legend of the Red Ruby”
body:
Sales company The Playmaker Munich has closed further territory deals on animated family adventure film “Pirate Mo and the Legend of the Red Ruby” ahead of the American Film Market, where it will have its market premiere. The film has now sold to more than 50 countries. Variety is debuting the teaser (below).

	The latest buyers for the film, helmed by “The Amazing Maurice” co-director Florian Westermann, include Umbrella Entertainment, who took rights for Australia and New Zealand, Israel’s FilmHouse and Vietnam’s Skyline Media.
	

	Previously announced sales include for the Baltics (Garsu Pasaulio Irasai), Benelux (Just4Kids), Bulgaria (Pro Films), Czech Republic and Slovakia (DonArt Production), Ex-Yugoslavia (Blitz), Greece (Rosebud.21), Hungary and Romania (ADS), Middle East (Grand Entertainment for Motion Pictures), Poland (M2 Films), Portugal (Outsider Films), Scandinavia (Njutafilms), Turkey (Filmarti), Ukraine (Svoekino) and North America (Viva Pictures Distribution).


	The distributor in Germany and Austria is DCM Distribution, with the theatrical release set for April 29, 2027.

	The screenplay for the film, which is based on Kirsten Boie’s novel “Seeräubermoses,” is written by Richie Conroy and Westermann.

	The film is set on board a pirate ship, on which a child, Mo, lives with a crew of ragtag seadogs and the ship’s pet … a goat. 

	Mo, who arrived by chance among the pirates as an infant, has been brought up by the ship’s kindly captain, Claas. One day, she is captured by the wicked pirate Peg Leg Olle, and meets the resourceful cabin boy, Hannes, and his pet bird. Together with Hannes, Claas, his motley crew and their pets, Mo will have to defeat Peg Leg Olle and fulfill her childhood prophecy of finding the Blood Red Ruby of Doom to restore peace and harmony to the land.
	

	The film is produced by Ulysses Films, Letterbox Filmproduktion, Isla Molona AIE, Arxlight Pictures and Arx Anima. The producers are Emely Christians, Sonja Matthes, Michael Lehmann, Holger Ellermann, Dunja Bernatzky, Kris Staber, Nicolás Matji and Edmon Roch.

	It is supported by ICAA, OEFI+, DFFF, MOIN Film Fund Hamburg Schleswig-Holstein, FFA, BKM, OEFI, ICEC, FFW and Creative Europe MEDIA Slate Funding.

schema.headline: ‘Pirate Mo and the Legend of the Red Ruby’ Sails to More Than 50 Countries Ahead of AFM Premiere as Teaser Debuts (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘The History Boys’ Returns to London West End After 20 Years, With Nicholas Hytner Back Directing Alan Bennett’s Play
description:
Alan Bennett’s “The History Boys” is going back to London’s West End after a 20-year absence. 

	Nicholas Hytner returns to the National Theatre pr
body:
Alan Bennett’s “The History Boys” is going back to London’s West End after a 20-year absence. 

	Nicholas Hytner returns to the National Theatre production he first staged in 2004, which later went to Broadway and won six Tony Awards there.

	Set in 1980s Britain, the comedy follows eight pupils at a Sheffield boys’ grammar school. They deal with adolescent desire, staffroom politics and teachers locked in an intellectual tug-of-war. Along the way the play takes on sexuality, growing up, what history actually is and what schooling is for.
	

	The run at the Theatre Royal Haymarket will begin previews on April 10, 2027 and close on July 24. Bob Crowley, who designed the original staging, returns as set designer. The cast will be revealed in January 2027.


	Hytner is producing with Brian and Dayna Lee, whose credits include “Giant.” That play won the Olivier for best new play and earned four Tony nominations on Broadway with John Lithgow. The three most recently partnered on “The Standard of Living.” Len Blavatnik and Danny Cohen also produce for Access Entertainment, with Mark Rubinstein as executive producer.

	The Lees said it was a privilege to return Bennett’s play to the West End with “the incomparable Nicholas Hytner once again at the helm.”

	“Bennett’s sharp, funny and deeply moving exploration of institutional culture, class and education feels as timely as ever. We can’t wait to share this remarkable production with a whole new generation,” they said.

	After its 2004 bow at the National, the play transferred to both the West End and Broadway. It won three Olivier Awards as well as the six Tonys, and its young ensemble went on to break out.
	

	“More than 20 years after it opened, it’s the right time to be bringing this great and much loved play back to the London stage. I can’t wait to take another look at it, and to introduce it to a new generation of theatergoers,” Hytner said. “My collaboration with Alan Bennett has been central to my creative life, and it’s a delight to be back in the theater with him again.”

	Bennett said: “’The History Boys’ is one of the happiest plays I’ve written. Or rather, it was one of the happiest of my plays to write. It was also one of the quickest to set down, taking far less than my usual five years. So, something of a record for me. The play is full of quotes and has itself become eminently quotable. A joy for any playwright. I welcome its return under Nicholas Hytner.”

	The Lees run AF Creative Media, whose Broadway credits include the Tony winners “Company,” “Moulin Rouge! The Musical” and “Angels in America.” The pair also hold a multi-year first-look deal with London’s Royal Court Theatre.

schema.headline: ‘The History Boys’ Returns to London West End After 20 Years, With Nicholas Hytner Back Directing Alan Bennett’s Play

title: Chris Pratt Confirms Star-Lord Will Return to the MCU, Says ‘Hard Action’ Has Been Taken to Make It Happen
description: Good news, “Guardians of the Galaxy” fans. Chris Pratt, who has played superhero Star-Lord across six films, recently confirmed that his character
body:
Good news, “Guardians of the Galaxy” fans. Chris Pratt, who has played superhero Star-Lord across six films, recently confirmed that his character will return to the MCU and that the studio has already taken “hard action” to make it happen.

	“I have a great relationship with Kevin [Feige] and Lou [D’Esposito], and there have been both ongoing conversations about how we make good on that promise and also hard action taken to make sure that we make good on that promise,” said Pratt on The Playlist’s “Bingeworthy” podcast while discussing Star-Lord’s comeback.
	

	He continued: “So yeah, you’ll see Star-Lord again, which is very exciting, but I’m not at liberty to say when that’s going to be, but he’s not going anywhere.”


	The news comes months after Pratt admitted he pitched Marvel an idea for bringing Star-Lord back into the MCU. “I’m happy to do anything they want me to do and will,” Pratt said about Marvel when on the “Happy Sad Confused” podcast. “And also, I personally have a really strong vision of what I would want him to do. And I think it’s fucking great.”

	When asked if he pitched this idea already to Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige, Pratt responded: “Yep. And I think that, you know, I’m down to contribute any way I can to them setting up the next 10 years of storytelling, you know? And also, I have a pretty strong idea of how I think I could contribute to that.”

	Pratt’s Star-Lord has appeared in “Guardians of the Galaxy,” “Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2,” “Avengers: Infinity War,” “Avengers: Endgame,” “Thor: Love and Thunder” and “Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3,” the latter of which promised via credits scene text that Star-Lord would return.
	

	The next installment in the MCU, “Avengers: Doomsday,” hits theaters on Dec. 18.

schema.headline: Chris Pratt Confirms Star-Lord Will Return to the MCU, Says ‘Hard Action’ Has Been Taken to Make It Happen

title: Netflix, Bengali Streamer Hoichoi Partner to Bring Series to Hindi, Tamil and Telugu Audiences
description: Every series Bengali streamer Hoichoi launches over the next two years will get Hindi, Tamil and Telugu-language versions streaming exclusively on
body:
Every series Bengali streamer Hoichoi launches over the next two years will get Hindi, Tamil and Telugu-language versions streaming exclusively on Netflix, under a partnership the two companies unveiled in Mumbai on Thursday.

	New titles will arrive on Netflix in the three languages at the same time as their Bengali debut on Hoichoi. The first is “The Cursed Temple of Kauriburi,” a horror series rooted in folklore that bows Nov. 6, with Jeetu Kamal, Solanki Roy and Paoli Dam in the leads. More releases will follow over the coming months.
	

	Netflix will also carry 14 existing Hoichoi series. The lineup comprises “Madam Inspector,” “Sampurna,” “Lajja,” “Eken Sirji,” “Anjaan Saaye,” “The Curse of Parnashavari,” “Bloodlines,” “The Adventures of Daadi & Jagga,” “Raat Abhi Baaki Hain,” “Achinta: Trial By Law,” “Shaadi Ka Siyappa,” “Queens,” “Parineeta: A Love Story” and “Mahanagar.” Genres run from crime thrillers and detective mysteries to folklore horror, social and courtroom drama, and romance.


	The two companies will also make new shows together. Netflix and Hoichoi will work on original series that rework selected Hoichoi stories, with Hoichoi Studios producing. The companies said each adaptation would bring in new creative voices. Further details have yet to be revealed.

	For Netflix, the pact is part of a wider effort to supplement its originals with more licensed programming from outside producers. The streamer said its global audience, which it puts at close to a billion people, gives studios, networks and creators a strong reason to work with it.
	

	The Hoichoi pact follows two other high-profile licensing moves. In France, Netflix now carries the full programming lineup of broadcaster TF1. In Brazil, Netflix struck a deal earlier this month with broadcaster Globo, which had long held out from licensing to the streamer in its home market even as its content appeared on Netflix elsewhere in Latin America and around the world.

	Hoichoi launched in 2017 as the first venture from SVF’s new media arm and is run by co-founder Vishnu Mohta, also SVF’s executive director. The platform hosts more than 2,000 hours of programming, among them over 100 original series, films, shorts and docuseries, and says it reaches more than 250 million Bengalis around the world. It moved into theatrical production in 2023, setting up Hoichoi Studios as its film production arm.

schema.headline: Netflix, Bengali Streamer Hoichoi Partner to Bring Series to Hindi, Tamil and Telugu Audiences

title: ‘Mother Bhumi,’ ‘Rehana Maryam Noor’ and ‘The Tourist’ Producers Head to Indonesia’s JAFF Market for New Exchange Program
description: Producers behind Fan Bingbing‘s “Mother Bhumi,” Cannes Un Certain Regard title “Rehana Maryam Noor” and BBC One and Stan drama “The Tourist” are am
body:
Producers behind Fan Bingbing‘s “Mother Bhumi,” Cannes Un Certain Regard title “Rehana Maryam Noor” and BBC One and Stan drama “The Tourist” are among 14 picks for the debut Producers Exchange at Indonesia’s JAFF Market, which will hold its third edition Nov. 28-30 in Yogyakarta.

	The market runs alongside the Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival (JAFF) and is sponsored this year by Amar Bank. It has set up the program to steer visiting producers toward Indonesian partners. Each participant will get a tailored calendar of pre-booked meetings with teams from the JAFF Future Project selection, rights holders from JAFF IP Connection, exhibitors and other delegates. Meetings will be matched to each producer’s background and interests, with conversations ranging from adaptation and financing to co-production and release.
	

	“We want international producers to see and experience Indonesia as a creative and production partner, with stories, talent and companies they can make films with,” said Linda Gozali, market director of JAFF Market. “Producers Exchange is designed to move those conversations towards joint development, financing and access to audiences, and to build partnerships that continue long after the market closes.”


	Malaysia’s Wong Kew Soon produced “Snow in Midsummer,” which won the Firebird Award for best film at the Hong Kong International Film Festival. He also produced “Mother Bhumi,” starring Fan, which picked up three Golden Horse Awards and played in Tokyo’s main competition. U.S.-based Rajib Mohajan, representing Bangladesh and the U.S., was a producer on “Rehana Maryam Noor,” which went to Un Certain Regard in 2021. He now develops films and documentaries through Studio Forty-Five Hundred.
	

	Singapore has two producers in the lineup. Sam Chua Weishi’s recent feature credits include Rafael Manuel’s “Filipiñana,” which played Sundance this year, and Nelicia Low’s Karlovy Vary title “Pierce.” Wendy Lie’s latest, Nelson Yeo’s “The House on the Moon,” competed at Locarno. Her first feature, Ang Geck Geck’s “Ah Girl,” took a special jury prize at Rotterdam this year.

	Taiwan’s Shao-Yi Chen, general manager of Screenworks Asia, was executive producer on the Taiwanese-Indonesian horror film and series “Losmen Melati.” Her drama series “Islanders” earned 10 nominations at this year’s Golden Bell Awards. South Korea’s Kimbo Kim, founder of Seoul- and New York-based outfit 37th Degree, produced the Korean-American feature “Abroad” and directed “Forte.”

	Representing Indonesia alone are Nana Riskhi and Nick Musa. Riskhi, a former Tempo TV CEO, is supervising producer on the Netflix Indonesian Original “General Mayhem: The Killing of Brigadier J.” Musa’s credits include “Death Knot” and “Orpa.” Thailand’s Phimphloi Nan Saensuk, known as Nan, works as a producer for IFA Bangkok after more than seven years at Sahamongkolfilm International. She is developing romantic vampire thriller series “Soulless” with director Anucha Boonyawatana.

	Rounding out the selection are Filipina producer Danzen Santos Katanyag, president of Digital Dreams International; Mongolia’s Otgontuya Zorig, CEO of Repeater LLC, who is producing music drama “Letter from Paris”; and Vancouver-based filmmaker Jason Karman, representing Canada and Indonesia, whose debut feature “Golden Delicious” played 62 festivals.

	The two Australians, Lisa Scott and Rae Choi, will come aboard via the market’s tie-up with the Adelaide Film Festival (AFF). Scott’s credits include “The Tourist,” made with U.K. company Two Brothers Pictures, as well as “Pine Gap,” “Wolf Creek” and “Janet King.” Choi, founder of Limina Pictures, produced Canneseries selection “Ina.” She is working with Robert Connolly on his upcoming feature “Shiver.”

	Mat Kesting, AFF’s CEO and creative director, said the tie-up offers Australian producers a focused way to build ties with Indonesian filmmakers and companies from the earliest stages of a project. “We hope these exchanges lead to films shaped by both countries’ creative perspectives, with partners who can help them reach audiences across Australia, Indonesia and the wider region,” he said.
	

	Each selected producer will get four nights’ lodging in Yogyakarta and accreditation for the market, along with entry to networking events and screenings and exposure on JAFF Market’s official platforms.

	JAFF was founded in 2006. This year’s festival will run Nov. 28-Dec. 5.

schema.headline: ‘Mother Bhumi,’ ‘Rehana Maryam Noor’ and ‘The Tourist’ Producers Head to Indonesia’s JAFF Market for New Exchange Program

title: Sebastian Koch, Toni Servillo Set for Oscar Winner Gabriele Salvatores’ Chess-World Noir ‘The Lüneburg Variation’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Sebastian Koch, star of Oscar-winning German film “The Lives of Others,” and Toni Servillo, protagonist of Italy’s Oscar winner “The Great Beauty,”
body:
Sebastian Koch, star of Oscar-winning German film “The Lives of Others,” and Toni Servillo, protagonist of Italy’s Oscar winner “The Great Beauty,” are set to topline “The Lüneburg Variation,” a noir based in the world of chess, directed by Gabriele Salvatores.

	Salvatores – himself also winner of an Oscar for “Mediterraneo” – has started shooting in Trieste on “Lüneburg Variation,” which is based on the eponymous novel by Italian author Paolo Maurensig that has been translated into 25 languages. Nine weeks of principal photography are planned between Trieste and Rome.
	

	The film will be distributed in Italy by RAI Cinema’s 01 Distribution while RAI Cinema International Distribution is handling international sales.


	The book opens with the suicide of a wealthy Munich businessman named Dieter Frisch near Vienna, leading to flashbacks of a revenge plot orchestrated through the game of chess.

	“It is the story of a duel that lasts more than 40 years, fought by two adversaries on the battlefield of a chessboard. Chess! The most violent sport in existence and, perhaps, the least cinematic. It’s a great challenge, and one I was happy to take on,” Salvatores said in a statement.

	The director added that he would delve into “the violent, magical, esoteric and mysterious dimension of chess, that is, instead, truly cinematic!”

	“Maurensig envisioned a film of half-light; darkness and fire. Compelling and cruel. I hope I can deliver just that…,” Salvatores went on to note.

	Rounding out the chess-world noir’s main cast are German actor Damian Hardung (“Maxton Hall”); Thomas Prenn, who is from South Tyrol and starred in Terrence Malick’s “A Hidden Life”; and Itay’s Eduardo Scarpetta (“My Brilliant Friend”).
	

	“The  Lüneburg Variation” is being lead-produced by Raffaella Leone and Andrea Leone through their Lotus Production, which is a Leone Film Group company, with RAI Cinema, in association with Vice Pictures and also in association with Italy’s Indiana and MDE.

	“We are very happy to be working with Gabriele Salvatores, a filmmaker and director we have always loved for the mastery with which he takes you by the hand and transports you into his world, making you fall in love with cinema all over again — real cinema, great cinema with a capital C,” Raffaella Leone said in a statement.

	Francesco Melzi d’Eril, Leonardo Maria Del Vecchio, Riccardo Volpato, Marco Cohen, Benedetto Habib, Fabrizio Donvito and Daniel Campos Pavoncelli are also producers on the film, which is being supported by the Friuli Venezia Giulia Film Commission.

	The key creative team on “Lüneburg Variation” comprises Diego Indraccolo as director of photography; Rita Rabassini as production designer; Patrizia Chericoni as costume designer; and Federico De Robertis as composer.



	

									Leone Film Group

schema.headline: Sebastian Koch, Toni Servillo Set for Oscar Winner Gabriele Salvatores’ Chess-World Noir ‘The Lüneburg Variation’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Dolly Parton CMA Tribute: Sabrina Carpenter, Julia Roberts, Oprah and More Remember the Country Icon as the ‘Great Unifier’
description: Sabrina Carpenter, Julia Roberts and Oprah were among the stars who paid tribute to Dolly Parton during the Country Music Association’s celebration
body:
Sabrina Carpenter, Julia Roberts and Oprah were among the stars who paid tribute to Dolly Parton during the Country Music Association’s celebration of the late country icon Wednesday night.

	Oprah, who appeared in a pre-recorded video at the beginning of the broadcast, shared what Dolly meant to her. “We’re both Tennessee girls, and she represented to me the essence of being 100% who you see yourself to be. Authentic all the time, and I just loved her for it,” she said. “I love that she had such grace and such tenacity. I mean, listen, if she put her mind to something, that was it. And I love that she was so generous of heart and generous of spirit, and her presence here on Earth will be felt for forever because the spirit that is so strong that was hers is actually everlasting.”
	

	Roberts, who starred alongside Parton in 1989’s “Steel Magnolias,” reflected on the experience of filming with the performer. “Dolly came into my life when I was in my early 20s, and it was magical to see someone so alive, so present,” the actress shared in a pre-recorded video. “She really was a shining example of remembering who you are, where you came from, and what it means to be kind. We love her.”


	Katy Perry took the stage to remember Parton as a woman who “masterfully toyed with the power of her femininity.” “Devastatingly sharp and equally as sweet, she could read you for filth with a wink and a smile, and then make sure that your children learn to read too. That’s a mother,” she continued. “Beneath the decades of dazzle was an extraordinary generosity of spirit. Some called her the Great Unifier because she had this ability to bring people together from all walks of life, political perspectives and sexual orientations. She saw beyond those labels because she saw the humanity in everyone. For me, Dolly is the blueprint.”
	

	Carpenter, who, before Parton’s passing, had collaborated with her on a remix of “Please Please Please,” said that the “I Will Always Love You” singer “meant lightness” as she began her recorded tribute. “She meant kindness, joy, quick comebacks, rhinestones, big hair, family, radiance, and love. I think Dolly was one of the only people on planet Earth that everyone could universally agree on, which I think is very special in any artist. But there’s nobody like Dolly.”

	Carol Burnett, who first met Parton while filming the 1979 CBS television variety special “Dolly & Carol in Nashville,” recalled an early memory of the star while on set. “When I talk about thoughtful, I remember there was one night I was in my hotel room getting ready to go out to dinner to a restaurant, and there was a knock at the door, and I opened it, and there was Dolly with a home-cooked meal for me, so that I wouldn’t have to go out to a restaurant, and to top it off, that home-cooked meal was home-cooked by Dolly herself.”

	Bono, Goldie Hawn and other stars also paid tribute to Parton during the show.

	The special was a “joyful, emotional celebration of the artist, songwriter, entertainer, humanitarian and entrepreneur whose music and generosity carried her from the mountains of East Tennessee into the hearts of generations around the world, told through performances, archival footage and personal stories that trace her extraordinary journey to becoming one of the most beloved entertainers and philanthropists in American history,” per the evening’s official logline.

	The singer-songwriter-actress died in August at the age of 80 following a “brief battle” with cancer.

	Over the course of the evening, more than 20 performers took the stage, including Ella Langley, Lainey Wilson, Reba McEntire, Carrie Underwood, Vince Gill, Kristen Bell, Molly Tuttle and Carly Pearce, as well as Kelsea Ballerini, Brad Paisley, Zac Brown, Ashley McBryde, Bela Fleck, Kristin Chenoweth, Lady A, Ricky Skaggs, Sierra Hull, Little Big Town, Lukas Nelson and Darius Rucker.

	The special aired live on ABC and Disney+ on Wednesday and will stream on Hulu the following day.

schema.headline: Dolly Parton CMA Tribute: Sabrina Carpenter, Julia Roberts, Oprah and More Remember the Country Icon as the ‘Great Unifier’

title: Indonesia Drafts New Film Law as Jakarta, Home to Four Netflix Productions, Courts International Shoots (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Indonesia’s film agency is helping draft a revised Film Law that would reshape its powers, while Jakarta, where Netflix now has four titles in prod
body:
Indonesia’s film agency is helping draft a revised Film Law that would reshape its powers, while Jakarta, where Netflix now has four titles in production, is working to become a regional film hub.

	Fauzan Zidni, chair of the Indonesian Film Agency (BPI), tells Variety the first draft, prepared with the Ministry of Culture, has taken shape since Cannes. “It is still in discussion, and I will say more when the moment is right, but the direction is right and the momentum is there,” he says.
	

	The Jakarta Film Commission launched in June alongside Filming in Jakarta, a one-stop service for producers. Karno says production companies from Malaysia and India have since come to the city to shoot films and series.


	In the capital, Netflix’s latest slate follows “Tygo,” the streamer’s “Extraction” spinoff. “We’re very happy to say that Netflix now is doing [four] titles … through Filming in Jakarta,” says Vice Governor Rano Karno. Under a memorandum of understanding tied to the inaugural Jakarta Film Summit, Netflix will also help develop local film talent, he adds.

	Governor Pramono Anung has set the goal of making Jakarta a film hub on the scale of Busan, and Karno, a veteran actor and filmmaker, has driven much of the city’s film policy. Over the next five years, he says, Jakarta wants to settle the full ecosystem, from production through financing and market access, and build Busan-style infrastructure. Post-production facilities, soundstages and studios are the biggest gaps, which the city aims to fill within three to five years.
	

	Jakarta has cut certain location fees by 50% and introduced a 50% tax concession on cinema admissions for qualifying Indonesian films. Karno says the city has barely scratched the surface on production incentives and is working to improve them, learning from Thailand and Malaysia as it tries to grow the industry faster.

	Busan has been a close partner. Karno credits the Busan Film Commission with helping the Jakarta Film Commission become an official member of AFCNet, the Asian Film Commissions Network. “It’s a momentum for us to be known [as the] future film hub in the region,” he says.

	To spread the benefits beyond the capital, the city is working with Bank Indonesia’s Jakarta representative office on the film and creative economy sectors, and is inviting filmmakers and industry players to its film summit and festival. Its Jaksinema initiative, which brings cinemas into public markets, offers cheaper tickets aimed at lower- and middle-income audiences.

	Karno, who says he has spent more than 50 years understanding the industry’s problems, expects the summit to become an essential date on the calendar, with the city government fully committed to making Jakarta a City of Cinema.

	The summit will also take on what Zidni sees as the core barrier to institutional investment. Banks lend against physical assets such as land, buildings and machinery, which production houses can’t offer. Film IP, including copyright and broadcast and distribution rights, has no valuation method that banks or the Financial Services Authority (OJK) will accept.

	Government Regulation No. 24 of 2022 on the Creative Economy already allows for IP-based financing. What’s missing are technical guidelines from OJK and a revision of OJK Regulation No. 40 of 2019 on asset quality so that IP can formally count as collateral. The summit is bringing OJK, the Ministry of Creative Economy, the Directorate General of Intellectual Property (DJKI), banks and the Indonesian Appraisers Association together to agree on a standard IP valuation method, a pilot financing scheme and a regulatory path.

	At the national level, Indonesia has no equivalent of France’s CNC, Korea’s KOFIC or Singapore’s IMDA. BPI can convene, advocate and coordinate, but it cannot fund films on its own or mandate policy. Zidni wants the revised law to give the agency statutory authority and ring-fenced funding.
	

	Two ministries currently oversee film in Indonesia, and Zidni says BPI is not trying to replace either of them. “That coordination problem is as much political as it is institutional, and solving it is part of the work,” he says. He calls the Minister of Culture’s support the strongest it has been in years, but gives no date for getting the law through parliament.

	Local productions took roughly 67% of Indonesia’s box office last year, though Zidni says 2026 is tracking at slower growth amid global economic pressures. “What we have not built is the bridge that carries those stories outward,” he says.

	At the Lumière Summit, Indonesia’s Ministry of Culture announced a new international co-production fund, developed with CNC support and open to filmmakers worldwide working with Indonesian partners. It sits alongside a matching fund, under which the government contributes up to a set ceiling per project for producers who land international financing. Zidni concedes that the matching fund on its own won’t help independent producers who lack overseas contacts.

	“What it does is create a concrete incentive to invest in building those relationships, the payoff is now tangible and government-backed, not hypothetical,” he says.

	Indonesia signed its first audiovisual co-production agreement, with the Netherlands, at JAFF Market in 2024. Talks on a bilateral treaty with France are active. Korean producers are looking hard at Southeast Asia, and Zidni calls Indonesia the obvious partner by scale, though he can’t give a precise timeline. “We are no longer asking partners to believe in our intentions,” he says.

	Zidni, who previously worked at Disney, watched global streamers pull back from Southeast Asian originals after 2023. “A platform can change its content strategy, exit a market, or deprioritize Indonesian content, and we have no recourse,” he says. BPI is pushing for closer ties with international sales agents and regional distribution within Southeast Asia, and is exploring whether Indonesian producers can build a shared market presence.

	Talent is another pressure point. Indonesia’s film schools, spread across 27 campuses, turn out around 1,200 graduates a year, but most are not absorbed by the industry and turnover runs at about 60%, Zidni says.
	

	His mandate runs to 2030. By then, he wants at least two bilateral co-production treaties in force, a financing system with a track record, and Indonesian producers attending the major international markets as regulars.

	“When the system works routinely, not heroically, that is when I will know we have built something that lasts,” he says.

schema.headline: Indonesia Drafts New Film Law as Jakarta, Home to Four Netflix Productions, Courts International Shoots (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘Petal Dance’ Director Ishikawa Hiroshi Ends 13-Year Feature Hiatus With ‘The Blue We Touch’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Japanese filmmaker Ishikawa Hiroshi, whose credits include “Tokyo.sora,” “Su-ki-da.” and “Petal Dance,” is back with his first feature in 13 years.
body:
Japanese filmmaker Ishikawa Hiroshi, whose credits include “Tokyo.sora,” “Su-ki-da.” and “Petal Dance,” is back with his first feature in 13 years. His new film, “the blue we touch” (original title: “Awo no Jo”), is in post-production and will be released in Japan in 2027 by Bitters End, which unveiled the project ahead of the Tokyo International Film Festival‘s TIFFCOM market.

	The ensemble drama centers on a pair of former friends and traces the hard-to-name feelings that pass between people. Nao heads the cast as Mitsu, 29, who does contract web design and wants a permanent job, along with a chance to make work that connects with an audience. She is drawn to Fujino (Nakajima Ayumu), who runs HR at her firm, and slowly starts to share grievances she has kept quiet about for a long time.
	

	Karata Erika plays Ayane, who works nights while preparing for a career as a public prosecutor. She crosses paths with Tomoki (Aoki Yuzu), an art student who can’t get his figure drawing right, and agrees to sit for him as a model. The arrangement opens up Tomoki’s work, while Ayane finds her way back to memories she treasures.


	Nakano Arisa, who made her screen debut in Wim Wenders’ “Perfect Days,” plays Nozomi, a classmate of Tomoki’s who watches him change up close.

	Ishikawa handled writing, directing and editing duties. He won awards as a commercials director before moving into features with “Tokyo.sora” in 2002. “Su-ki-da.” followed in 2006 and earned him best director at the New Montreal FilmFest, with “Petal Dance” arriving in 2013. His work is known for its careful handling of color and its feel for the mood of ordinary days.
	

	Nao’s earlier films include “The Last 10 Years” and “Sensei’s Pious Lie.” Karata has appeared in “Asako I & II,” “Desert of Namibia” and Netflix’s “The Queen of Villains,” while Nakajima’s credits span TBS’ “Until the T-Shirt Dries,” “Happyend” and “Wheel of Fortune and Fantasy.” Aoki’s résumé includes “5 Centimeters per Second,” “Blue Lock” and “Minamata.”

	Bitters End has been active for more than three decades, releasing films in Japan by Hamaguchi Ryusuke, Bong Joon-ho, the Dardenne brothers, Jia Zhangke, Roy Andersson and Gianfranco Rosi. Its recent releases include “Below the Clouds,” “Young Mothers” and “The Odyssey.”

	On the production side, the company’s credits include Oscar winner “Drive My Car” and Locarno Golden Leopard recipient “Two Seasons, Two Strangers.” This year, “All of a Sudden,” which took a prize at Cannes and is Japan’s Oscar submission for international feature, played in competition, and “All the Lovers in the Night” made the Un Certain Regard lineup.

	Bitters End is now growing its international sales operation. “In My Father’s Room” competed at San Sebastián, where it took the Fipresci Prize and the Ateneo Guipuzcoano Award.

title: John Anderson, Country Hall of Famer Whose Hits Included ‘Seminole Wind’ and ‘Swingin’,’ Dies at 71
description:
John Anderson, the country Hall of Famer behind hits like “Seminole Wind” and “Swingin’,” has died. He was 71.

	Anderson’s death was announced by
body:
John Anderson, the country Hall of Famer behind hits like “Seminole Wind” and “Swingin’,” has died. He was 71.

	Anderson’s death was announced by his family across his social media accounts on Wednesday. No cause of death or further information was noted.

	“It is with the heaviest of hearts that we share the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and best friend,” read the statement. “To the world, he was a gifted country music singer whose voice and songs touched countless lives. To us, he was so much more. He was the heart of our family, the one who made us laugh, loved us fiercely, and made every ordinary moment feel special.”
	

	It continued: “We are completely heartbroken. His music will live on, but for us, his greatest legacy will always be the love he gave his family and the memories we will carry with us forever. Please keep our family in your thoughts and prayers as we grieve this unimaginable loss.”


	Over Anderson’s nearly five-decade career, he earned 20 Top Ten country hits, with five reaching the top spot on the charts — “Wild and Blue,” “Black Sheep” and “Swingin’” were among his most notable hits, as were “Straight Tequila Night,” “Money in the Bank” and “Seminole Wind.” From his first, the self-titled debut “John Anderson” in 1980, to his last, “Years,” released in 2020, the country singer released 22 studio albums.

	Anderson was inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame in 2024 and previously into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2014. He won the Academy of Country Music Career Achievement Award in 1993.
	

	“John Anderson was a one-of-a-kind song stylist who proved that fresh innovations were best born from time-honored traditions,” said Kyle Young, CEO of the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum, in a statement. “Whether he borrowed inspiration from Lefty Frizzell’s vocal bends or the Florida swamp land, he brought dynamic distinction and creative soul to a world that needed to hear his voice. In 1981, John famously gave life to Billy Joe Shaver’s lyric, ‘I’m just an old chunk of coal, but I’ll be a diamond someday.’ He was already a diamond then, and a diamond he always will be.”

	Anderson was born Dec. 13, 1954, in Orlando. He grew up in Apopka, Fla., and knew by age twelve that he wanted to pursue music. After graduating from high school, he moved to Nashville, began performing regularly, and ultimately signed a recording contract with Warner Bros. Records in 1976.

	He is survived by his wife, Jamie, their two daughters, Alexa Kate and Brionna Cheri, and his grandchildren.

            Sarah Palin's asking her followers to send prayers Ron Duguay's way amid his cancer battle.
      
    
            The former Vice Presidential candidate took to her Instagram story Sunday to share photos of her boyfriend in his hospital bed, leaning on her faith during this tough time.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            One photo shows Sarah holding the former NHL star's hand, which she captioned ... "Prayers for Ron Duguay so appreciated."
      

            She shared another image of her and Ron looking at each other while he lays in bed with a tube in his nose.
      
    
            The text over the photo reads ... "I know God can. I'm asking Him to. And even if the answer looks different, I know by now to still hold on to Him."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            His daughter, Shay Thomas, also called for prayers earlier this month, posting her own photo from her dad's bedside.
      
    
            Ron's been battling stage IV colon cancer after getting diagnosed in 2024, and is being treated at City of Hope in Southern California.
      
    
            He revealed his diagnosis back in February. He and Sarah have been together since 2022.

            Ilhan Omar is addressing the longstanding allegation she married her brother to commit immigration fraud.
      
    
            During an interview with MS NOW's Chris Hayes, the Minnesota congresswoman was asked whether her former husband, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, is actually her brother, responding, "Not to my knowledge."
      
    
            Omar also called the allegations "insane," pushing back against claims surrounding her 2009 marriage to Elmi. The allegations have circulated for years, though no evidence has publicly established that Elmi is her brother.
      
    
            The interview comes after federal agents raided Omar's Washington, D.C., home on October 12 as part of an ongoing criminal investigation.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Trump has denied involvement in the raid, while the Justice Department says agents executed a judicially authorized search warrant.
      
    
            According to Reuters, investigators are examining whether Omar or members of her family made false statements in immigration paperwork dating back decades.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Omar has denied wrongdoing and accused President Donald Trump's administration of using the investigation to intimidate her ahead of the midterm elections.

title: Police Body Cam Shows Moments Before Cop Fatally Shoots 1-Year-Old Boy
description:
Mississippi Fatal Shooting
                          Cop Says He Didn't See Baby After Fatal Shoo
body:
Mississippi Fatal Shooting
                          Cop Says He Didn't See Baby After Fatal Shooting
                          ... Caught on Body Cam
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 21, 2026
                            7:15 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Newly released bodycam footage shows the chaotic moments leading up to a Mississippi police officer fatally shooting a 1-year-old boy during a suspected shoplifting incident at Walmart.
      
    
            The disturbing video captures officers rushing into the parking lot of a Senatobia Walmart on June 14 after receiving reports that two women suspected of stealing diapers and baby clothes were fleeing the store.
      
    
            The footage shows the women getting into a gray sedan with 1-year-old Kohen Wiley inside as officers approach the vehicle and repeatedly order the driver to stop.
      

            The car reverses into a parked SUV before accelerating forward, appearing to drive toward officers. At least one officer then opens fire as the vehicle passes between them.
      
    
            Kohen, who was sitting in his mother Vellesiya Wiley's lap, was struck by gunfire and killed. The driver, Latoya Ferrell, was also shot and critically injured.
      
    
            In the body cam recording obtained by Darkhorse Press, an unidentified officer is heard saying, "I didn't even see a f***ing baby in her lap."
      
    
            Another officer responds, "Nobody knew the baby was there."
      
    
      
      The Mississippi Attorney General’s Office announced it found an officer’s use of force was justified in the fatal shooting of 1-year-old Kohen Wiley. How can anyone accept that conclusion when Kohen’s family and the public still have not been allowed to see the body-camera footage?   
This is a department whose chief was fired after reports of racial slurs in his text messages, and whose officer faced a complaint alleging a racially offensive remark two days before he shot Kohen. If the footage supports the state’s decision, release it. We will not stop fighting until this family gets the truth. https://t.co/NXjFDwNDrq
              @AttorneyCrump
          
  
    
            The footage surfaced just days after Mississippi Attorney General Lynn Fitch's office announced the officer's use of deadly force was justified and that no criminal charges would be filed.
      
    
            Civil rights attorney Ben Crump, who represents Kohen's family, has slammed the decision and demanded the release of all footage surrounding the shooting.
      
    
            The newly surfaced videos do not include body cam footage from the officer who fired the fatal shots.

Ex-JPMorgan Exec
                          I'm Receiving Threats, ‘Vile’ A.I.-Generated Content
                          Over Banker’s Sexual Harassment Claims
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The JPMorgan exec being sued for alleged sexual harassment by an ex-JPMorgan banker says she's tired of dealing with “vile” jokes about her as she battles her accuser in court ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            According to court docs, obtained by TMZ, the exec, Lorna Hajdini, claims she cannot even walk down the street “like a normal human being” due to the false claims brought by the banker.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            She says she has been waiting for over a year to “clear her name” over the claims made by John Doe.
      

            Lorna is opposing the banker’s attempt to delay the case … insisting he has no evidence to support his “callous and fabricated allegations against her.”
      
    
            She says the banker and his legal team have been trashing her in the press for months … and claims she has received “countless lewd and threatening messages and has been the ongoing focal point of incessant jokes, memes and AI-generated content of a persistently vile, degrading and sexual nature – all because of [the banker’s] lies.”
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Lorna says she is in therapy … adding that every delay in the case is a nightmare for her. She's asking the judge to deny the banker's request for an extension of certain deadlines in the case so things can get moving.
      
    
            As TMZ previously reported, the banker sued Lorna, claiming he was subjected to “abhorrent sexual abuse.”
      
    
            For her part, Lorna countersued the banker for defamation. She claimed his lawsuit was full of nonsense, designed to ruin her reputation and shake down JPMorgan for millions.
